General Adult

$50.00 
(

General Youth
 (All day ticket - Ages 5-12):

(

Children under 5: FREE
2026 Twilight Admission, 3:00pm to 6:00pm entry, sales beginning November 1:
A great excuse to visit the Dickens Fair for a second time for shopping, dinner or a show!
Adult Twilight Ticket
 (entry after 3 pm): 
$35.00 
($41.04 total*)
Child Twilight Ticket
 (entry after 3 pm): 
$20.00 
($25.51 total*)
2026 Active Military Discount
Active Military:
 1st & 2nd Weekends 
FREE
 Admission
Active Military personnel along with three family members will receive FREE Admission on our First and Second Weekends!
(Nov. 21, 22, 27, 28, 29; photo I.D. required at Will Call.)
No reservation or ticket is required. Just go to the Will Call window with your active ID and they will assist you. Remember that children under 5 never need a ticket and do not count toward the 4 free tickets. Thank you and your family for your service.
The 2026 Pickwick Club Season Pass
Join the Pickwick Club and count yourself among the merriest of Christmas Keepers. With the purchase of a season pass you can become a member of this illustrious club. The 
2026 Season Pass
 price is 
$200.00 
($211.81 total*) (over $600 in value!).
By ordering a Pickwick Club season pass, you will receive with our sincere compliments:
A Pickwick Club membership card.
Admission to all 11 days of the 2026 Dickens Christmas Fair (excluding parking), and 10% off all items purchased at the "Patterson & Sons" Fair memorabilia store and other participating locations displaying the Pickwick Club insignia.
Free coat and parcel check.
Experiences
Visitors can enrich their Victorian holiday with epicurean adventures and mysteries to solve in these curated 
Experiences.
Port and Chocolate Tasting
A delicious adventure into the romance and fantasy of Port wine, a true Victorian favorite, paired with 
Bramosia Chocolates
.
Gin Tasting
The dangerous and delicious history of Gin, including 
tastings of different types and a choice of cocktail from one of the selections
.
Jekyll and Hyde Pub Crawl
Solve the mystery and bring Mr. Hyde to justice while imbibing custom designed elixirs at four London pubs.
The Dark Garden Corset Experience
Lace up in luxury with world-renouned corsetiere 
Dark Garden
. Includes complimentary sparkling wine, and store credit. Purchase or simply photograph & dream.
Important Ticket Information:
Tickets are good for any one date of the event of the 2026 season.
In order to control attendance and maintain comfort within the event on busy days, tickets will not be sold on site. 
All tickets must be purchased ONLINE ONLY
. We recommend that you plan to come early in the day and early in the season!
Please be aware that ALL tickets are NON-Refundable
. Although non-refundable, tickets are fully 
transferable
, and can be gifted to any person of your choosing.
Season Passes are not transferable, and must be presented with a photo I.D.
Parking fees are charged at the entrance to the lot by the Cow Palace. The Cow Palace charges $20 per vehicle for parking. (Please email us about large vehicle parking.)
Wheelchairs: The Fair is accessible. Wheelchairs are available for rental at the Cloak and Parcel Check inside the Lower Lobby for $15.00 per half day (4 hours) or $30.00 per full day (4+ hours) on a first-come, first-served basis.
For general questions about the event, please refer to our 
FAQ
 page.
If you still have event or ticket related questions, please email 
[email protected]
.
Legal Bits
Tickets may not be sold for cash on Fair premises. In accepting a ticket, the holder releases Fair owners and management, the Cow Palace, and Agricultural District 1-A, from all liability in the event of accident, property damage, or theft while on Fair premises. Holder grants permission to The Great Dickens Christmas Fair and its agents to utilize ticket holders’ (and their minor children’s) likeness or image incidental to any live or other recording.
Red Barn Productions reserves the right to refuse admittance to any customer not only based on its discretion, but also for health safety or other reasons such the customer being unruly, disrupting the business or its operations, causing injury, stress, or upset to employees, contractors or other customers.
Happy Holidays!
“There is nothing in the world so irresistibly contagious as laughter and good humor.”
~ Charles Dickens, A Christmas Carol

2026 is our 52nd year
selling trees!
Open in 1974, Santa’s Tree Farm and Village in Half Moon Bay, CA, is a 487-acre Choose-and-Cut Christmas tree farm with 4 different kinds of trees. We give you the saw and send you off to find the perfect tree! Visit Santa’s Village for fun holiday activities. Trees up to 13 feet tall in the field for 2026! Pre-cut trees up to 9 feet tall available in the barn.
Free candy canes and visits with Santa with every tree purchase, while supplies last.

Tellabration! ™
Hosted by 
John W.
Super Organizer
@ Menlo Park Library
Details
Our Storytelling Festival concludes with a whole lot of tale-spinning!
Tellers from the South Bay Storytellers and Listeners will be joining us to share their 35th annual Tellabration™ event. Join us to listen, or perhaps to contribute a tale, yourself!
This storytelling event targets adults, but school-age children accompanied by an adult are welcome.
Tellabration
™ is worldwide event of storytelling created in 1988 by Connecticut storyteller J.G. Pinkerton. The event brings people together and shares the power and joy of storytelling.
South Bay Storytellers and Listeners are a network of people in Silicon Valley dedicated to making storytelling a vital part of the community. The group hosts the monthly Silicon Valley Storytelling Meetup, now taking place on the 4th Tuesday evening of each month at Menlo Park Library!
This is one of nine events in the 
11th Annual Menlo Park Storytelling Festival
. Join us for one event, or the whole series!
Sun. Sept. 27 | 
Clara Kamunde: Afri-Crafty Tales
 | Belle Haven Library | All ages |

Roopa Mohan presents Kasturba Gandhi

Jeff Gere: True Supernatural Tales of Hawaii
 | Menlo Park Library | 9-Adult |
Sat. Nov. 21 | 
Tellabration!
 ™ | Menlo Park Library | 5-Adult |
About Storytelling:
Storytelling is telling stories--without using a book.
It's an ancient art form that predates libraries, and books, and writing.
It's not necessarily for children!
Traditional-style storytelling creates unique images in the mind of each listener.
According to the 
National Storytelling Network
, "storytelling is the interactive art of using words and actions to reveal the elements and images of a story while encouraging the listener’s imagination. In storytelling, the listener imagines the story.”
According to the 
Storytelling Association of California
 (an organization dedicated to promoting storytelling as a living art form), storytelling is “orally passing on adventures, wisdom, experiences, surprise, history, laughter, beliefs and imagination.”

 Purisima Creek Redwoods Preserve
Approximate Total Miles
 2
Image
 Hike
It's that time again: The banana slug count! Join Docent Naturalists Roberta and Jaime Cavazos and Melissa Hero on this family-friendly, leisurely-paced search for everyone’s favorite local, golden gastropod. As you meander beneath the redwood canopy along the Purisima Creek Trail, you’ll count and learn about these amazing creatures and where they live. Bring a light snack to enjoy along the trail. 
Reservations are required and will be accepted on or after November 7 at 12:00 p.m. (Noon) and close November 20 at 2:00 p.m.
 Where to Meet
From the North: Accessible from Purisima Creek Road. From the Highway 92 and Highway 1 intersection in Half Moon Bay, travel on Highway 1 south approximately 4.3 miles. Turn left on Verde Road. After turning on to Verde Road and traveling 1/4-mile, continue straight to remain on what becomes Purisima Creek Road. (Verde Road splits off to the right.) Travel approximately 3.7 miles on Purisima Creek Road. From the South: Accessible from Purisima Creek Road. From the Highway 84 and Highway 1 intersection in San Gregorio, travel on Highway 1 north approximately 6.4 miles. Turn right on the third Verde Road intersection. After turning on to Verde Road and traveling 1/4-mile, continue straight to remain on what becomes Purisima Creek Road. (Verde Road splits off to the right.) Travel approximately 3.7 miles on Purisima Creek Road.

 Windy Hill Preserve

 Hike
‘Tis the season to learn about what natural gifts late fall brings such as the berries and nuts found growing wild in the local habitats. On this leisurely-paced, family-friendly hike with Docent Naturalists Olga and Tony Bright, you’ll explore around Sausal Pond on the Spring Ridge and Betsy Crowder trails looking for these fruits and considering the various ways they’ve been used in human cultures. (Note: Foraging is prohibited on protected lands; this activity is for interest/information/fun only.)
 Where to Meet
The Lower Windy Hill Parking Area at the lower portion of the preserve is located on Portola Road. Please note: This parking lot fills quickly. Please do not park on Portola Road: parking is strictly enforced.

Thanksgiving 5K Fun Run
Parks and Recreation
Thanksgiving 5K Fun Run
Next date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 | 09:00 AM 
 to 11:30 AM
The 53rd annual South San Francisco Thanksgiving 5K Fun Run will take place on 
Saturday, November 21, 2026
 at the Oyster Point Marina & Bay Trail. 
The run will begin at 9:00 a.m
.
The Fun Run is a great way for community members of all ages to get moving and enjoy the outdoors! Whether you’re ready to race for your best time or prefer a relaxing walk with family and friends, everyone is welcome to participate along the scenic Bay Trail. Runners and walkers of all ages and abilities are encouraged to join the fun. Please note: dogs, scooters, bicycles, and skates are not permitted on the course.
Participants will be awarded prizes for top finishers in each age group.  All participants who register are entered into an opportunity drawing for prizes. Winners are pre-drawn and will be notified by email to pick up their prize at the conclusion of the race.
Save Time with Early Bib & Shirt Pick Up!
Bibs and shirts will be available for pick-up on the following dates and times at the Library | Parks and Recreation Center (901 Civic Campus Way, South San Francisco) on the 3rd floor.
Thursday, November 19 from 8:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m.
Friday, November 20 from 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.
Note: If you are picking up a bib / shirt for a friend or family member, you must present a copy of their registration receipt. Shirts are available only for those who registered and purchased a shirt by November 1.
Children ages 5 and under will not receive a bib.

sfco-nutcracker-sweet.text:
FAMILY CONCERTS 2026-27 Season
From our annual Nutcracker “Sweet” to our new Sensory Friendly Family Concert, you’ll be sure to find something for the whole family. And, just like the rest of our concerts, they are entirely…
ADMISSION FREE!
RSVP’s are NOT required but it helps us to know you’re planning to attend!
Nutcracker “Sweet” 
Featuring 
The Puppet Company
Oakland Fairyland’s beloved puppeteers team up with the SFCO for a delightful version of Tchaikovsky’s holiday classic. Designed for young audiences, this production features the acrobatic antics of The Puppet Company’s miniature cast accompanied by the SFCO performing highlights from this beloved ballet. A firebreathing dragon, confetti and a show-and-tell of the different puppet types highlight this 40 minute gem. Join us for this joyful Thanksgiving Weekend tradition!
Please note 
our admission free concerts have an open seating policy on a first come, first serve basis. 
Doors open an hour before showtime and guests will be welcomed in until the space reaches capacity.

The SFCO is excited to present our 
fourth year of Sensory Friendly concerts
, specifically designed with our neurodivergent community in mind.
What does that mean? ALL are welcome and every type of engagement with the music is encouraged. We’ll refrain from sudden loud sounds, our All-Star String Quartet performs at a beautifully pleasant volume, we'll have a basket of fidget toys, and the seating will create plenty of space for movement and expression.
The instruments of the string quartet will be introduced and we'll present a variety of musical styles ranging from classical gems to popular favorites. And for extra engagement, throughout the program we'll have fun, hands-on activities for those who wish to participate.
Our concerts are always Admission Free! Please RSVP so that we know you're interested!
